title: Circuit breaker on Kubo HTTP API
description:
Wrap all Kubo HTTP RPC calls in a circuit breaker so a slow or unreachable Kubo node degrades the service gracefully rather than hanging every inbound NNTP connection.

Why this issue exists:
Kubo is a required external dependency. If it becomes slow or unreachable, every NNTP command that touches the block store (ARTICLE, POST, BODY) will hang waiting for an HTTP timeout. Without a circuit breaker, a Kubo outage cascades into a full service hang rather than a clean error response to clients.

Scope:
- Wrap KuboHttpClient (in core/src/ipfs/mod.rs) with a circuit breaker (tower or a lightweight hand-rolled state machine)
- States: Closed (normal), Open (failing fast), Half-Open (probe recovery)
- Thresholds: configurable failure rate and window (default: 5 failures in 10 seconds opens the circuit)
- When Open: block_put and block_get return Err immediately without making an HTTP call; NNTP returns 403/503 to the client with a human-readable message
- Recovery probe: one request allowed through every N seconds (default 30) to test if Kubo is back
- Emit a structured log event and increment a Prometheus counter on state transitions (closed->open, open->half-open, half-open->closed)
- Circuit breaker state is per-daemon-instance, not shared across processes

Acceptance criteria:
- With Kubo stopped: after threshold failures, subsequent block_get calls return immediately with an error, no HTTP timeout wait
- Prometheus metric kubo_circuit_breaker_state{state=open} increments on transition
- When Kubo restarts, the circuit closes within one probe interval
- NNTP clients receive 403 with message 'block store unavailable' when circuit is open, not a timeout hang
